scenario.description: An investment committee chair must authorize a company's commitment to a private credit fund and set the eligibility, reporting, and liquidity conditions for signing, with input from compliance and fund operations.

shared_context.S1: The company is considering a $6,000,000 commitment to Northbridge Private Credit Fund IV.
shared_context.S2: The fund invests in senior secured corporate loans and accepts commitments until the end of the month.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding decision on whether and on what conditions the company will sign the commitment agreement.
shared_context.S4: As part of the committee's routine pre-signing review, Elena asks compliance and fund operations to report any issues and execution requirements before deciding.
shared_context.S5: The committee records exact dollar amounts and required pre-signing or pre-funding actions in its decision, and may approve the commitment conditionally using documented commitments.

PF1.text: Jonas received a policy amendment in this morning's compliance circular that caps the company's commitment to this fund strategy at exactly $5,000,000, requires qualified-purchaser certification before signing, and requires quarterly look-through reporting; the amendment has not yet been circulated to the investment committee.

PF2.text: Maya received the fund administrator's confirmation today that the first capital call will be exactly $1,200,000 within 5 business days after signing, and treasury can ring-fence that amount in cash. The confirmation states a fixed dollar figure and does not scale proportionally if the commitment amount is reduced; it has not yet been added to the committee packet.

acceptance_conditions: The commitment amount must be exactly $5,000,000.
Qualified-purchaser certification must be required before signing.
Quarterly look-through reporting must be required.
Exactly $1,200,000 must be ring-fenced in cash for the first capital call.
The settlement must include a commitment whose detail references ring-fencing or cash reservation of $1,200,000 for the first capital call.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'pre-funding' and c['target'] in ['treasury', 'Maya'] and (('$1,200,000' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('1,200,000' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('1200000' in c.get('detail', ''))) and (('Ring-fence' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('ring-fence' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('Ring fence' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('ring fence' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('reserve' in c.get('detail', '')) or ('Reserve' in c.get('detail', ''))) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The $6,000,000 proposal otherwise appears executable, but PF1 changes commitment_amount_usd to exactly 5,000,000 and adds the certification and quarterly look-through requirements that make approval compliant.

Without PF2, the committee has no confirmed fixed first-call amount or cash-availability basis, so it would not set capital_call_cash_reserve_usd to exactly 1,200,000 or require a pre-funding commitment whose detail records ring-fencing or reserving that exact amount.
